title: Want to see shooting stars? This October meteor shower doesn't need a latenight wakeup
excerpt: Draconids is at its best and brightest in the evening, just after it becomes dark. Here's what it means, when and how to watch it
content:
Oct. 3, 2026, 5:08 a.m. ET

Most meteor showers are famous for peaking just before dawn, providing spectators with breathtaking views of a glimmering night sky. But there lies the caveat –– to catch the showers at their very best, you usually have to wake up at an ungodly hour and let your eyes adjust to the dark for at least 30 minutes before you can enjoy the view.

The Draconids meteor shower, which peaks next week, is an exception to this trend. Draconids is at its best and brightest in the evening, just after it becomes dark, according to Space.com. This means your schedule doesn't have to completely unravel to get a glimpse of it.

Here's everything to know about the Draconids meteor shower.

What is the Draconids meteor shower?

Also known as Giacobinids, the Draconids are one of two annual meteor showers observed in the month of October. Meteor showers occur as the Earth passes through a cloud of cometary debris –– in the case of the Draconids specifically, they come about as the planet passes through the Comet 21P/Giacobini-Zinner.

The shower originates from a point in the Draco constellation, giving it its name.

The Draconids aren't a particularly prolific shower, and magnificent outbursts are rare, but you might catch a glimpse of some meteors and comet debris nevertheless. The most active displays of the 20th century produced by the Draconids happened in 1933 and 1946, according to Royal Museums Greenwich.

Where can I see the Draconids meteor shower?

Skies across the Northern Hemisphere will light up with Draconids, but the intensity depends on the clouds that night. To get the best view, try to find a spot that is unobstructed by the horizon and offers a clear view of the stars.

There is no distinct advantage of using a telescope or binoculars, just try to be in a spot where you get as wide a view of the sky as possible.

What is the best time to watch the Draconids meteor shower?

The Draconids will be on display between Oct. 6 through Oct. 10 and peak in the evening hours of Oct. 8 and Oct. 9 at about 9 p.m. To catch the best view, you can keep an eye out for them after sunset, as soon as it turns dark.
